The finding asserts an 'attack surface' and 'misconfiguration determines whose credentials get exercised' without any concrete exploitable path grounded in the changed code, making it speculative noise rather than a verifiable defect or a specific actionable advisory.

judged_text: teamDestinationCalendars is populated via a side effect inside the teamMemberPromises map and only for COLLECTIVE events, so a ROUND_ROBIN event's destinationCalendar array stays single-element while the same unscoped credentialId values flow to createAllCalendarEvents. Users booking collective events write events to every host's personal destination calendar, and because those destination rows carry credentialIds consumed without ownership checks (EventManager.ts), the attack surface for cross-user credential use grows with each host added to an event type; behavior also silently differs for ROUND_ROBIN, so event-type misconfiguration determines whose credentials get exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends each teammate’s `user.destinationCalendar` via a side-effect (`teamDestinationCalendars.push(...)` inside `users.slice(1).map(...)`) and then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` (handleNewBooking.ts). That feeds into `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, which now iterates every `destination` and, if `destination.credentialId` is present, will fetch an arbitrary credential by id from the DB (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })`) and use it to call `createEvent` without any ownership/team scoping checks. This expands cross-user credential usage surface area as more hosts’ destination calendars are added. Also, ROUND_ROBIN does not add team destination calendars (only COLLECTIVE does), so behavior differs by eventType scheduling configuration as described.
